issues.failure_explanation: Eliminating G and G^3 from A_0+A_1G+A_2G^2=0 and its shifts gives A_0^{(1)} = -A_0 A_1^{-1} A_0 and A_2^{(1)} = -A_2 A_1^{-1} A_2. The recursion as written omits both minus signs. With the written formulas the identities in eq:crqme, and the formula for G in terms of \widehat A_1^{(k)}, are false already at k=1. The recursion therefore does not generate the CR sequence the paper relies on.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the minus signs in the updates of A_0^{(k+1)} and A_2^{(k+1)}.
issues.overall_effect: The invariant-subspace extraction and convergence statements use identities that do not hold for the sequence as defined. The implementations (SMCSolver) presumably use the standard signs.
issues.title: CR recursion has wrong signs for A_0^{(k+1)} and A_2^{(k+1)}, contradicting the stated identities
issues.why_classification: A local, forced sign correction restores all claims. It is borderline with a pure typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The first hypothesis contains the product S_2 A_2 with S_2 of size q x q and A_2 of size m x m, which is undefined. It also does not match the paper's own application. Section 3 sets S_1^{-1}=\Lambda_{R,1} and U_1=T_{R,1}, where the available relation is \Lambda_{R,1}^2 T_{R,1}A_0+\Lambda_{R,1}T_{R,1}A_1+T_{R,1}A_2=0. The required hypothesis would be U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0, which is not what is stated. The conclusion also says the eigenvalues of S_1^{-1} are moved to infinity, whereas the pole of the left factor, and the application, move the eigenvalues of S_1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the left condition as U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0 and correct the statement of which eigenvalues move to infinity.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated cannot be applied to the setting of Section 3, so the hypotheses used there are not those of the quoted result.
issues.title: Hypothesis of the block shift theorem is dimensionally ill-formed and inconsistent with its use
issues.why_classification: A local restatement consistent with the cited result and Section 3 suffices. No argument changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Section 3 obtains \widetilde A(z), its coefficients and the factorization by applying Theorem th3.2 (and th5) with S_1^{-1}=\Lambda_{R,1}. That theorem requires det S_1 != 0, i.e. \Lambda_{R,1} nonsingular. \Lambda_{R,1} has eigenvalue 1/lambda_j = 0 whenever A(z) has an eigenvalue at infinity (A_2 singular), as in Example 1 where lambda_8=infinity. The paper discusses singularity of \Lambda_{G,1} but never that of \Lambda_{R,1}. The formula (I+zT^T(\Lambda_R^{-1}-zI)^{-1}T) is then undefined, and the deflated factorization and the QMEs for \bar G, \bar R are not justified by the cited theorems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Give a direct verification, or a continuity or rewritten version of the shift theorem expressed in \Lambda_{R,1}, valid when \Lambda_{R,1} is singular.
issues.overall_effect: The reduced equations (22), (23) and the BS-CR algorithm are unsupported by the stated theory in the case A_2 singular, which includes the paper's own first test problem.
issues.title: Shift theorems invoked with S_1=\Lambda_{R,1}^{-1} even though \Lambda_{R,1} may be singular (e.g. Example 1)
issues.why_classification: A contained extra argument fills the gap and the method and results survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims lim Null(A_0^{(k)}) = lim Null(A_2^{(k)}) = m-l. Zeros of det A^{(k)}(z) tending to 0 do not make A_0^{(k)} exactly singular. If all lambda_i are nonzero, each A_0^{(k)} is a product of nonsingular matrices and has nullity 0 for every k. The proof only gives A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1} -> 0, i.e. at least m-l singular values tend to 0. It never shows that the remaining l singular values stay bounded away from 0 (sigma_l(A_0^{(k)}) does not vanish). That is exactly what is needed for the span of the trailing right singular vectors V_{0,2}^{(k)} to converge to span(W_{G,1}), and for the test sigma_{l+1}/sigma_l < eps to be eventually satisfied. The following statement rank(W_{G,1}) = lim rank(V_{0,2}^{(k)}) is vacuous, since V_{0,2}^{(k)} always has m-l orthonormal columns.

failure_location.quote: has exactly $m-\ell$ zeros that converge to 0, which implies that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the nullity statement by a singular-value statement and prove that sigma_l(A_0^{(k)}) and sigma_l(A_2^{(k)}) are bounded away from 0, with the resulting subspace convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification of the SVD-based subspace identification, and of the stopping criterion in Algorithm alg:isg, is missing. The convergence of the subspace and of \widetilde\Lambda^{(k)} is asserted rather than proved.
issues.title: Nullity claim is false/unsupported; rank-gap of A_0^{(k)} needed to identify the invariant subspace is not proved
issues.why_classification: Requires a new contained lemma on the singular-value structure of A_0^{(k)}, A_2^{(k)}. The method and its advertised guarantees are retained.

issues.failure_explanation: For A_2^{(k)}=U_2 Sigma V_2^T, the vectors u with u^T A_2^{(k)} ≈ 0 are the trailing columns of U_2, so the rows of T_{R,1} should be the transposes of those columns, i.e. T_R=U_2^T. The text and algorithm instead partition U_2 into row blocks and take the last m-l rows of U_2 as T_{R,1}. Those rows do not give T_{R,1}A_2^{(k)}≈0 in general. The output specification also lists sigma(\Lambda_{R,1}) with the index m+l instead of m+l+1, which is inconsistent with an (m-l)x(m-l) matrix, and the formulas use \widehat A_1^{(k+1)} for G but \widehat A_1^{(k)} for R.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define T_R=(U_2^{(k+1)})^T, with T_{R,1} the last m-l rows of T_R. Fix the index and the iteration index in the formulas.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the computed T_{R,1}, \Lambda_{R,1} and hence the deflation of R are incorrect.
issues.title: Left invariant subspace of R taken from rows of U_2 instead of columns (missing transpose)
issues.why_classification: A short convention fix restores the procedure without new arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is the only solution to \eqref{eq:qmeGbar} with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$

issues.failure_explanation: The pencil (M,N) built from B_0,B_1,B_2 has 2l eigenvalues, all of modulus 1, namely each mu_i twice with a one-dimensional eigenspace (a Jordan block). The sought solution corresponds to an l-dimensional deflating subspace containing exactly one copy of each mu_i. The algorithm computes an unordered generalized Schur form and takes the leading l columns. Nothing is said about reordering the eigenvalues, and there is no modulus criterion to separate the wanted subspace. The output claim (eigenvalues mu_1..mu_l) is therefore not guaranteed. The sensitivity of the defective double eigenvalues is not discussed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a reordering step (e.g. reordered QZ selecting one copy of each mu_i, which are known in the QBD case) with an argument that the leading block gives the required deflating subspace.
issues.overall_effect: The QZ step of BS-CR is not well specified, so correctness of \bar G_{11} (and then \bar R_{11}, G, R) is not guaranteed.
issues.title: QZ-based algorithm does not specify how to select the deflating subspace for one copy of each double unimodular eigenvalue
issues.why_classification: Needs a contained additional construction (ordered Schur selection plus justification) rather than new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the condition for the non-singularity of the matrix $\bar{A}_{122}$ is

issues.failure_explanation: The B_i in eq:Bbar contain \bar A_{122}^{-1}, and \bar G_{21}, \bar R_{12} also need it. The algorithm computes B_i unconditionally, then guards only the last computation with an 'if \bar A_{122} nonsingular' that has no else-branch, after which G and R are formed from \bar G_{21}, \bar R_{12}. Nothing in the assumptions guarantees nonsingularity. The paper only says it is equivalent to nonsingularity of T_{R,1}A_0W_{G,1}, and only when \Lambda_{G,1} is nonsingular. When \Lambda_{G,1} is singular (lambda_1=0, as in Example 1) no analysis is given. For singular \bar A_{122} the algorithm is undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove nonsingularity of \bar A_{122} under the stated assumptions, or add it as an explicit hypothesis, or give an alternative procedure for the singular case. Make the algorithm flow consistent.
issues.overall_effect: BS-CR does not have a guaranteed input-output contract under the stated assumptions. Its applicability rests on an unverified condition, contrary to the claims of a broad class and reliable convergence.
issues.title: Nonsingularity of \bar A_{122} is never established, yet BS-CR needs it unconditionally
issues.why_classification: A hypothesis or contained argument and a corrected algorithm flow keep the method. The scope claim is slightly narrowed if the condition must be assumed.

issues.failure_explanation: In Table 1 the residual of CR is 4.4e-16, smaller than BS-CR's 3.9e-15. The text says BS-CR is clearly the most accurate, and the introduction says it is much more accurate than classical CR from the numerical experiments. For Example 1 the table shows the opposite.

failure_location.quote: Concerning residual error, \texttt{BS-CR} is clearly the most accurate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the statement to say the accuracy is comparable in Example 1, with BS-CR's accuracy advantage shown only in Examples 2 and 3.
issues.overall_effect: The accuracy claim for Example 1 (and the general introduction claim) is not supported by the reported data; only the iteration-count advantage is.
issues.title: Claim that BS-CR is most accurate contradicts Example 1 table (CR has smaller residual)
issues.why_classification: Local rewording, with no change to methods or proofs.

issues.failure_explanation: For l=8 the listed values contain 1 twice and -1 twice. Then G_{11} has these eigenvalues repeated, so 1 and -1 are eigenvalues of A(z) of multiplicity 4, not 2. The kernel of A(mu) is then 2-dimensional, contradicting the uniqueness assumption of Section 2.2. The paper acknowledges only the complex-entries deviation. The uniqueness of \bar G_{11} and the QZ selection argument no longer apply in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose l=8 distinct unimodular mu_i (e.g. 8th roots of unity), or state that Case 3 is outside the theory.
issues.overall_effect: The Case 3 results do not test the method within its assumptions, so they cannot support the robustness claim for l=8.
issues.title: Example 3, Case 3 uses repeated mu_i, violating the distinctness and multiplicity-2 assumptions
issues.why_classification: Only the numerical test data needs correction. The theory is unaffected.
